page: Amazon Web Services r8in.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture operating at 3.9 GHz. The hardware configuration delivers 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with 2 threads per core, alongside a substantial 480 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is provisioned at 512 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory rated at 7 GHz, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The instance includes 100 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and contains no bundled local storage or integrated GPUs.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate robust parallel compute and data delivery capabilities. The system achieved a multi-core stress-ng score of 69,171.31 and an uncached read memory bandwidth of 192.67 GB/sec, placing it within the top 25 percent of tested systems. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 441.21 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput peaked at 151.09 GB/sec, placing it in the top 10 percent tier. For transactional in-memory workloads, it recorded 115.14 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. Furthermore, hardware-assisted matrix capabilities like AMX and AVX-512 support strong small-to-medium CPU-based LLM inference throughput, achieving 297.08 prompt processing tokens per second on 7B models.

Resource allocation presents clear qualitative tradeoffs. The high memory density and 100 Gbps network pipe provide immense throughput per instance, reducing the operational overhead of horizontal scaling for massive memory footprints. However, the absence of local NVMe storage requires external EBS volumes for persistence, which must be factored into storage architectural planning. Single-core compute and large 70B parameter LLM generation scale moderately compared to its parallel strengths.

AWS r8in.16xlarge is strategically suited for high-density in-memory caching solutions, enterprise databases, real-time analytics engines, and CPU-driven vector processing pipelines that rely heavily on DDR5 throughput and high-speed network communication.
